dossier_meta.statement_text: For each proper hereditary family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs there are $C_{\mathcal{F}},d_{\mathcal{F}}>0$ such that if $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, every graph on $n$ vertices which is $\varepsilon^{d_{\mathcal{F}}}$-close to $\mathcal{F}$ contains an $\varepsilon$-homogeneous set of size at least $\varepsilon^{C_{\mathcal{F}}}n$.
dossier_meta.context_text: A graph on $n$ vertices is $\alpha$-close to a family $\mathcal{F}$ if one can add or delete at most $\alpha n^2/2$ edges to obtain a graph in $\mathcal{F}$. This conjecture, introduced as a natural extension for hereditary families, defines the polynomial close Rödl property; a family with this property also has the polynomial Rödl property.
